design.affected_system: coastal protection, evacuation, and long-term adaptation system
alternatives: phase evacuation by official risk zone
prioritize carless and assisted populations before general departure
adapt closure and evacuation timing to ensemble tracks and observed network state
assumptions: Elevation, surge, shoreline, asset, and population layers share documented vertical and horizontal datums.
Sea-level pathways, damage functions, and adaptation performance remain explicit scenarios.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: Current fixed evacuation and closure triggers remain in effect.

constraints.description: Each phase must satisfy clearance time, transport capacity, worker safety, and public-notice lead time.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: event-triggered and reviewed at the stated decision horizon
design.decision_owner: coastal resilience director and emergency-management commissioner
design.decision_question: When should ports, roads, services, and evacuation zones transition before a coastal storm?

independence_key.binding_constraint: Each phase must satisfy clearance time, transport capacity, worker safety, and public-notice lead time.
independence_key.decision_object: phased coastal closure and evacuation timetable
independence_key.evidence_gate: Validated demand, route capacity, transit schedules, control points, and disruption states support clearance estimates.
independence_key.primary_outcome: population remaining in risk zones at unsafe conditions

design.intended_claim: A versioned schedule design for comparing declared alternatives affecting phased coastal closure and evacuation timetable, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: population remaining in risk zones at unsafe conditions
distributional gap in population remaining in risk zones at unsafe conditions
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not call simulated clearance an actual evacuation result or assume universal compliance.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Validated demand, route capacity, transit schedules, control points, and disruption states support clearance estimates.

design.title: Schedule coastal closures and phased evacuation
transportability_risks: Coastal morphology, tides, subsidence, protection standards, and evacuation behavior differ.
Long-horizon adaptation values depend on local finance, land tenure, and legal authority.
